policySummary.accountValueTooltip: This is the cash value amount held within the owner's life insurance policy. The account value accumulates over time as premiums are paid and interest is earned.
policySummary.surrenderValueTooltip: This is how much the owner or their payees can expect if the policy is surrendered. It's the current account value minus surrender charges, outstanding loans, and other fees.
policySummary.baseDeathBenefitTooltip: This is the death benefit amount related to the owner's base coverage. It reflects the current figure, so it accounts for any changes to the death benefit that have occurred due to withdrawals or loans. (Note: This figure may differ from total gross death benefit if there are additional lines of coverage or riders that add to the death benefit.)
policySummary.gracePeriodTooltip: These dates tell you how long the owner has to make the required grace payment to keep the policy active. The first date is when the policy went into pending lapse status, and the second is the deadline to make the required grace payment.
policySummary.gracePeriodMinPaymentTooltip: This is the minimum amount the owner must pay in premium before the grace period ends to keep their policy active (and their coverage and account value intact.)
policySummary.lapseEffectiveDateTooltip: This is the date when the policy lapsed. The owner didn’t make a grace payment, so now the policy is officially inactive.
policySummary.reinstatementPeriodTooltip: This tells you how much time following lapse date the owner has to begin the process to reinstate the policy. Some policies don't have a reinstatement period. In that case, a lapsed policy has ended for good.
policySummary.underwritingDecisionTooltip: Lapsed policies must be approved via underwriting to be reinstated. During underwriting, the carrier assesses the risk of insuring the owner based on their health and lifestyle and determines the cost of their insurance. Once approved, the owner may make the required payment to get their policy back to active.
policySummary.reinstatementPaymentPeriodTooltip: These dates tell you how long the owner has to make the required reinstatement payment once approved via underwriting. The first date is when the owner was approved for reinstatement, and the second is the deadline to make the required reinstatement payment.
policySummary.reinstatementMinPaymentTooltip: This is the minimum amount the owner must pay in premium within the reinstatement approval period to get their policy back to active.

policyDetails.amountRemainingUntilCurrentGuidelineLimi: Amount remaining until current guideline limit

coverageSideSheet.baseDeathBenefitTooltip: This is the death benefit amount related to the owner's base coverage. It reflects the current figure, so it accounts for any changes to the death benefit that have occurred due to withdrawals or loans. (Note: This figure may differ from total gross death benefit if there are additional lines of coverage or riders that add to the death benefit.)
coverageSideSheet.coverageChangeUnitTooltip: The owner can change their coverage in units of this amount. For example, if their coverage change unit is $100, they can increase or decrease coverage by $100, $200, and so on.
coverageSideSheet.minCoverageAmountTooltip: This is the lowest amount that an owner can reduce their death benefit to. Less coverage may lead to lower premiums—and negative tax consequences. If the decrease creates a large enough gap between the death benefit and the premiums paid in, the policy may fail guidelines tests and cease to offer tax advantages. All changes reset the seven year period for the 7-pay test.
coverageSideSheet.maxCoverageAmountTooltip: This is the highest amount that an owner can increase their death benefit to. Increase requests must go through the underwriting process for approval. All changes reset the seven year period for the 7-pay test.
coverageSideSheet.availableDecreaseTooltip: The owner may decrease their death benefit by this amount.
coverageSideSheet.availableIncreaseTooltip: The owner may increase their death benefit by this amount.
